legend: The tumour is well circumscribed, with a glistening cut surface.
Low-grade myxoid liposarcoma with abundant myxoid matrix forming mucin pools.
The typical plexiform, capillary size vascularization is seen. Neoplastic cells are cytologically bland. Monovacuolate lipoblasts are present. Low-power view.
Myxoid liposarcoma occasionally may show extensive mature fat maturation mimicking lipoma.
A hypercellular, poorly differentiated round cell population is seen that tends to obscure the underlying plexiform vascular network. Rare lipoblasts are seen.
Strong nuclear immunoreactivity with DDIT3 antibody on immunohistochemistry.

Axial MRI of the left lower leg of a 35-year-old woman. MRI features are typical for myxoid liposarcoma. The lobulated mass returns high signal on T2-weighted MRI (A) due to myxoid content that can mimic a cystic lesion. However, enhancement (T1-weighted fat saturation MRI postcontrast) in areas of increased cellularity/vascularity suggests complexity (B). T1-weighted MRI demonstrates T1 bright strands (C, arrow) that do not suppress following fat saturation (D, arrow), suggesting that these represent haemorrhagic foci. Although foci of fat (T1-weighted bright strands that suppress on fat saturation) can occasionally be seen within myxoid liposarcomas, these features are not present in this case.
source: Prof Christina Messiou, Royal Marsden Hospital, London, UK.
